surface_mechanism_description: ALD conformality over surface topography includes rounded as well as sloped regions, leading to the emergence of growth fronts where there is a significant change in incline on the surface, causing directional growth fronts and eventual merging of growth fronts at crossing points between inclined and curved regions.
evidence: While other physical or chemical deposition mechanisms convey some measure of conformality over topography, ALD’s self-limiting chemistry provides unprecedented capacity to maintain conformality even in the most challenging nanotopography. Side wall deposition (i.e., on the inclined surfaces) is as rapid as on the rounded surfaces. This causes the rise of directional growth fronts where there is a significant change in incline on the surface (i.e., shift from the sloped side walls to that of the concave valley or dimple).
